ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A $3 \times 4 \times 5$ cuboid consists of 60 identical small cubes. A termite eats its way along the diagonal from $P$ to $Q$. This diagonal does not intersect the edges of any small cube inside the cuboid. How many of the small cubes does it pass through on its journey?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a rectangular prism composed of unit small cubes, and the grid lines show that it is divided into small blocks. Point P is marked near one upper rear right vertex of the rectangular prism, and point Q is marked near the opposite lower front left vertex, so PQ represents the space diagonal passing through the rectangular prism. Reasoning: The problem gives the dimensions of the rectangular prism as 3 × 4 × 5. When moving along the body diagonal from P to Q, the termite will pass through internal grid planes perpendicular to the three directions. The numbers of internal planes in the three directions are respectively 3 - 1 = 2, 4 - 1 = 3, and 5 - 1 = 4. The termite is initially located in one small cube; each time it passes through an internal face plane, it enters a new small cube. The problem states that this diagonal does not pass through any edge of an internal small cube, so it will not pass through two planes at the same time, and no extra correction is needed. Therefore, the number of small cubes passed through is 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10.

raw_record.question_text: A $3 \times 4 \times 5$ cuboid consists of 60 identical small cubes. A termite eats its way along the diagonal from $P$ to $Q$. This diagonal does not intersect the edges of any small cube inside the cuboid. How many of the small cubes does it pass through on its journey?

method.method_draft: First read the diagram as a rectangular cuboid subdivided into unit cubes, with P and Q at opposite vertices and the segment PQ intended as the body diagonal through the cuboid. From the text, use the dimensions 3 by 4 by 5, so moving from P to Q the termite must cross the internal grid planes perpendicular to each of the three directions. There are 3-1=2 internal planes in one direction, 4-1=3 in another, and 5-1=4 in the third. The termite starts in one cube, and each time it crosses one internal face plane it enters exactly one new cube. The given condition that the diagonal does not intersect any small-cube edge ensures no two such plane crossings happen simultaneously, so no special correction is needed. Therefore the number of cubes passed through is 1+2+3+4=10.
